name: Lower Salish Sea
region: Lower Salish Sea, Washington State (USA) + British Columbia (Canada): Puget Sound, Admiralty Inlet, San Juan and Gulf Islands, Strait of Juan de Fuca to Cape Flattery, and the southern Strait of Georgia up to the Tofino / Nanaimo line
subject: Southern Resident + Bigg's (transient) killer whales and their forage web (Chinook salmon, Pacific herring, harbor seal)
client: Internal (personal side project; no client commitment)
brief: A hex-based ecosystem map that shows WHY orcas are where they are, then alarms when a fresh sighting lands near me so I can go see them. Rather than plotting dots, it models the forage web: Chinook and Pacific herring as the prey base, harbor seals as Bigg's prey, and the two orca ecotypes derived from their respective prey (Southern Residents from Chinook, Bigg's from seals). Real reported sightings (live from Acartia) sit on top as ground truth and drive a model-vs-reality diff. Forage layers are deterministic seasonal models (calendar x spatial prior), explicitly synthetic, not live data. This reuses the ecosystem-mapping-agent engine (Leaflet + h3-js) and extends drayton-harbor's Pacific-NW data catalog (NOAA, NANOOS, WA DNR) to the full lower Salish Sea. Config-driven: this file is the locked config the generic tool reads via ?site=salish-sea. Nothing north of Tofino.
_context_bounds_note: Full lower Salish Sea regional extent used for the bathymetry-driven grid and the open-water migration layers. `bounds` above is the summer SRKW focus (San Juans / Haro Strait); this is the whole map. North cap 49.2N = Tofino / Nanaimo line; south 47.0N = Olympia / South Puget Sound; west -125.5W = Tofino / Cape Flattery / outer Juan de Fuca; east -122.0W = Seattle / Bellingham shore. Excludes the upper Strait of Georgia.
_grid_note: LOCKED DECISION: dual grid. The engine's default single nearshore band (res 10, bathymetry-subdivided to 11) is kept for shoreline ecology but scoped to named zones only (herring spawn beaches, seal haul-outs) so it does not explode over hundreds of km of coastline. A coarse open-water grid (res 6-7, zoom-bump to 8) fills the channels and straits for the pelagic/migration layers (salmon, orca) and for bucketing sightings, because orcas and migrating Chinook travel open mid-channel water the nearshore band never covers. Each layer declares which grid it renders on.

nearshore.scope: named zones only (spawn beaches, haul-outs), not the whole coastline

time.note: Weekly scrubber; salmon/herring run timing turns over inside a month.

_layers_note: The five map layers. value is per-hex, per-week intensity in [0,1] (relative, not counts). model layers are deterministic seasonal calendar x spatial prior. See inputs for provenance/sources.

layers.label: Pacific herring
layers.note: Model-only, no live data, per requirement.

layers.label: Reported sightings
layers.note: Ground truth; feeds model-vs-reality diff + proximity alarm.

location.desc: Center + focus bounds + regional context_bounds that scope every layer to the lower Salish Sea.

water_mask.attribution: Natural Earth 1:10m coastline or OSM water polygons
water_mask.desc: Land/water polygon used to mask H3 cells to marine/estuarine only, once at config-build time. Without it both grids paint the Olympics and Vancouver Island. First thing to wire given the large land fraction of context_bounds.

bathymetry.source: NOAA NCEI Puget Sound / Salish Sea DEM
bathymetry.attribution: NOAA NCEI Bathymetric Data Viewer / Puget Sound DEM (same US source as drayton-harbor)
bathymetry.desc: Seabed depth. Drives the nearshore-band subdivision and helps delineate channels for the open-water grid.

salmon_runs.attribution: WA Dept of Fish & Wildlife + Fisheries and Oceans Canada run-timing and escapement; Chinook marine-distribution literature
salmon_runs.desc: Deterministic seasonal model: run-timing calendar x marine-distribution spatial prior (Fraser/Skagit approaches, Haro/Rosario, river mouths). Chinook primary (SRKW staple); other four as toggles. Synthetic by design, parameterized from data, not streamed.

herring_spawn.source: WDFW herring stock assessment + DFO herring spawn index
herring_spawn.attribution: WDFW Puget Sound herring stock assessments + DFO Pacific herring spawn index
herring_spawn.desc: Model-only per requirement (no live feed). Spawn-timing calendar x spawn-beach / holding-ground prior (Cherry Point, southern Gulf / San Juan shorelines). The forage base under everything. Nearshore band.

seal_haulouts.attribution: Harbor-seal (Phoca vitulina) haul-out inventories (WA DNR, DFO), pupping-season timing
seal_haulouts.desc: Haul-out density x pupping-season bump. Feeds the Bigg's orca layer. Nearshore band.

orca_presence.attribution: Derived: SRKW ~ f(Chinook), Bigg's ~ f(seal); calibrated to known seasonal patterns (NOAA SRKW, The Whale Museum)
orca_presence.desc: Not an independent dataset: the two orca layers are functions of the prey layers, so the map reads causally. Calibrated against published SRKW / Bigg's seasonal presence.

sightings.attribution: Acartia data collective (aggregates Orca Network, Ocean Wise Whale Report, Orcasound hydrophones)
sightings.desc: The only real-data layer. Polled every 2-5 min, bucketed to the open-water grid, rendered as time-decaying markers, and used for the proximity alarm and the model-vs-reality diff. Minutes-to-hours old and crowdsourced: a lead, not a fix. De-dupe by time+location; default filter to orca.

my_location.desc: Live device position for the proximity alarm and the radius ring. Never leaves the client.

_outputs_note: What running the tool on the inputs generates. Forage/orca layers are synthetic models; sightings + alarm are live.

forage_web_map.label: Forage-web hex map
forage_web_map.attribution: Astraeus deterministic seasonal models on Pacific-NW priors
forage_web_map.desc: The stacked prey layers over the season: what the orcas are eating and where.

orca_opportunity.label: Orca opportunity (SRKW + Bigg's)
orca_opportunity.attribution: Derived from prey layers, calibrated to NOAA SRKW / The Whale Museum
orca_opportunity.desc: Approximate presence for each ecotype, driven by its prey. The map's thesis layer.

sighting_feed.label: Live sighting feed
sighting_feed.desc: Real reports on top of the model, plus a diff layer highlighting where sightings and the model disagree.

proximity_alert.label: Proximity alarm
proximity_alert.attribution: Astraeus Action layer (client-side MVP; server push in phase 2)
proximity_alert.desc: Fires (sound + Web Notification + banner) when a fresh orca sighting lands within the distance threshold and freshness window of my location. Phase 1 is foreground-only; phase 2 adds asleep-phone push via ntfy/Pushover/Web Push.
